modern: Loss is nothing else than change. But the universal nature delights in change, and in obedience to her all things are now done well, and from eternity have been in the same form, and will be so for time without end. What, then, do you say—that all things have been and always will be bad, and that no power has ever been found among so many gods to set these things right, but the world has been condemned to be bound in never-ending evil?
original: Loss is nothing else than change. But the universal nature delights in change, and in obedience to her all things are now done well, and from eternity have been in like form, and will be such to time without end. What, then, dost thou say,—that all things have been and all things always will be bad, and that no power has ever been found in so many gods to rectify these things, but the world has been condemned to be bound in never ceasing evil?
notification: Loss is nothing else than change.
notification_original: Loss is nothing else than change.

explained.summary: Losing something is just a change, and change is how nature works. Through it everything happens as it should, as it always has and always will. Would you really claim that the world has always been bad, and that none of the gods has ever been able to put it right, so it’s stuck forever in misery? Marcus finds that far less believable than accepting change as good.
